subject: physiology
title: Hypoxia, high altitude and environmental physiology

steps.tx: **Hypoxia** divides into hypoxic with low arterial oxygen at altitude, anaemic with low content but normal pressure, stagnant with low flow in shock, and histotoxic where cyanide poisons mitochondria, sensed by carotid chemoreceptors driving acclimatisation by erythropoietin and two three diphosphoglycerate. Oxygen carriage follows the sigmoid dissociation curve shifted by Bohr effect, stored by myoglobin and delivered as cardiac output times content, blueing as cyanosis near five grams of deoxygenated blood. Curves therefore shift before tissues starve.
steps.say: Only one of four hypoxias lowers arterial oxygen pressure: hypoxic hypoxia at altitude, while anaemia lowers content, shock lowers flow, and cyanide blocks cellular use, compared in the types table. Carotid bodies sense true hypoxaemia and drive erythropoietin and curve shifts that unload oxygen to tissues. Pulse oximetry can look normal in three types, and five grams of deoxygenated haemoglobin blues the lips.

vis.alt: Table of four hypoxia types: hypoxic with low PaO2 such as altitude, anaemic with normal PaO2 but low oxygen content, stagnant with normal PaO2 and low flow as in shock, histotoxic with normal PaO2 where cells cannot use oxygen as in cyanide poisoning.
vis.caption: Only hypoxic hypoxia has a low PaO2; the other three have normal PaO2, so pulse oximetry can mislead.

steps.tx: **Altitude illness** above twenty five hundred metres headaches and nauseates as acute mountain sickness, ataxically confuses as cerebral oedema needing dexamethasone, and crackles as pulmonary oedema needing nifedipine or sildenafil, all cured by descent, prevented by acetazolamide and staged ascent sleeping low. Athletes live high and train low against erythropoietin doping bans, cabins pressurise near eight thousand feet needing supplemental oxygen in lung disease, and cold hypothermia rewarms against frostbite rewarmed with aloe. Heads therefore swell while lungs leak until descent.
steps.say: Headache and nausea after rapid ascent are signalling acute mountain sickness, unsteadiness and confusion are signalling cerebral oedema, and breathlessness with crackles is signalling pulmonary oedema, the three rows of the illness table. Descent is curing all three, dexamethasone is helping the brain, nifedipine is helping the lungs, and acetazolamide with staged sleeping is preventing illness. Athletes chase the same erythropoietin rise by living high and training low.

vis.alt: Table of high altitude illness: acute mountain sickness with headache and nausea treated by rest and acetazolamide, high altitude cerebral oedema with ataxia and confusion treated by descent and dexamethasone, high altitude pulmonary oedema with dyspnoea and crackles treated by descent and nifedipine.
vis.caption: Descent is definitive for all three; acetazolamide prevents AMS, dexamethasone treats HACE, nifedipine treats HAPE.

steps.tx: **Diving** squeezes by Boyle law on descent and reverses on ascent, narcotises by nitrogen rapture at depth, seizes by oxygen toxicity, bubbles joints as decompression bends needing staged table stops and definitive recompression chambers. Drowning spasms the larynx with hypothermia needing rescue breaths and warming, heat strokes past forty confused needing ice cooling and exhaustion needing salts and rest, and malignant hyperthermia needs dantrolene, while hydration with water breaks sustains. Pressures therefore dissolve gas before bubbles tear.
steps.say: Pressure rises one atmosphere every ten metres, halving gas volume at ten metres by Boyle law in the depth plot, which squeezes sinuses down and expands bubbles up. Nitrogen narcotises deep divers, oxygen can convulse, and missed decompression stops bend joints until a chamber recompresses. Drowning, heat stroke cooled with ice, heat exhaustion rested with salts, and malignant hyperthermia treated with dantrolene complete the immersion and heat family.

vis.alt: Plot of absolute pressure and relative gas volume against diving depth: pressure rises by one atmosphere per 10 metres of sea water, so a gas volume halves at 10 metres and falls to a quarter at 30 metres, following Boyle law.
vis.caption: Pressure adds one atmosphere per 10 m; air in the lungs and sinuses halves at 10 m, which drives barotrauma and bubble formation on ascent.

steps.tx: **Aviation and space** pull G forces against G-suits and straining, float weightlessly losing bone against exercise, radiate against shielding, and spin motion against scopolamine, with noise needing plugs, vibration whiting fingers, and pollution needing masks by air quality index. Circadian rhythms shift by melatonin and light timing. Suits therefore strain while masks guard and lights reset clocks, and records document exposures for crews routinely after every mission profile flown.
steps.say: Pilots fight G forces with suits and straining, astronauts lose bone without loading exercise, radiation needs shielding, and motion sickness answers to scopolamine, grouped in the environment table. Noise and vibration injure ears and fingers without plugs and gloves, polluted air needs masks, and light with melatonin resets shifted circadian clocks. Each exposure has a physical countermeasure matched to its mechanism.
